tb21_profile.skill: Author a correct nginx configuration from prose: a custom log_format using named variables, access_log/error_log paths, limit_req_zone in the http context with limit_req in the server block, error_page for a custom 404, a document root and listen port — then validate with nginx -t, disable the default site and bring the service up
tb21_profile.domain: nginx / Linux web-server administration: /etc/nginx layout, sites-enabled vs conf.d, request logging, per-IP rate limiting
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service: install, write config into the right files and contexts, create content, syntax-check, restart and verify over HTTP

verifier_notes: Terminal-Lego is the strongest domain match in the pool but also where the FREE grades cluster: task_02361, task_02282, task_02217, task_02254, task_11803 and task_02208 are all directly on-topic nginx-config tasks and all FREE, so none of them appears anywhere in my lists. notes: This is the task where the two new corpora most clearly beat the old pool, but in opposite ways. Terminal-Lego has roughly 177 nginx-configuration tasks — far more than the rest of the pool combined — and its best ones (log_format editing, error-log formatting, default-server shadowing, sites-enabled symlinks) are strongly verified and hit sub-requirements nothing else in the pool covers. It is also where the FREE problem bites: six directly on-topic nginx tasks in this shortlist alone are FREE and had to be dropped. CalibForge contributes the systems half: nginx-won't-start debugging with strong verifiers, and one Apache task that demands a disabled default site plus a named custom log format with User-Agent, which is the single closest match for the logging requirement outside TMax. TMax still supplies the two best overall candidates because they are the only tasks in the pool that require writing limit_req_zone and limit_req by hand. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld both offer the right task_form (install, configure, start, verify a web server) but almost always Apache/LAMP provisioning rather than config authoring, and RTS is entirely 'absent'-graded, so neither reaches the final ten. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench are judged on skill/domain only, as instructed: django-axes (per-IP and per-user-agent throttling) and waitress (header-text fidelity) are the honest transfers.
